thread:
mike: Quick heads-up — we need to provision a small bring-up pool in eu-west3 for the new customer pilot. Who's owning GPU quota requests and reservation?

anika: I can lead the quota request. Need to confirm target GPU SKU and expected qps. Is this A100 or H100?

mike: Pilot only needs throughput for inference testing: prefer A100-80GB if available; fallback to A100-40 or H100 if procurement blocks. Start with 8 GPUs for smoke, 32 for full soak.

cheng: FYI GCP eu-west3 has limited on-demand H100s. For A100 we should request quota across two regions (eu-west3 + europe-west1) to avoid single-region hot spots. Also need to reserve project-level compute.googleapis.com/acceleratorQuota.

sarah: Can we reserve via a commitment or just quota increase? Committed use is for billing; we want capacity reservation for the bring-up window (2 weeks) — prefer a short-term reservation request with cloud sales.

mike: Good note. Let's do both: request quota increase and ask cloud rep to pin capacity for 14 days. Template below that I used last time:

anika: Please paste template.

mike: ```
Subject: Request for temporary GPU capacity reservation
Project: redwood-prod-bringup-<team>
Region: europe-west3
Start: 2026-05-04T09:00Z
End: 2026-05-18T18:00Z
Requested SKUs/Counts: A100-80GB: 8 (initial), 32 (soak)
Fallback SKUs: A100-40GB, H100-80GB
Reason: New customer pilot requiring low-latency inference tests and load soak to validate autoscaler and KV cache behavior.
Billing contact: infra-billing@redwood.ai
Point of contact: anika@redwood.ai, +1-555-0102
Testing requirements: steady-state 200 rps for 3 hours, peak 1k rps burst.
Additional ask: capacity pin / reservation for 14 days or equivalent guaranteed provisioning.
```

cheng: That's solid. Add network details: VPC name, subnets, peering with customer VPN, and a tag for default firewall rules. Also include requested public IPs for NAT gateway if the cluster needs external access during bring-up.

mike: Good call. Update template with VPC: vpc-bringup-eu-west3, subnets: 10.40.0.0/20, peering: prod-customer-peering, nat: 2 ephemeral eips.

infra-bot: deploy-plan triggered by mike at 1812345685 — created bringup ticket INF-4521. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521

anika: For the IAM/KMS side: ensure service account redwood-bringup-sa has roles/compute.admin, roles/iam.serviceAccountUser, and access to KMS key redwood-eu-kms for model artifacts. Request KMS access window in the ticket.

ops-oncall: We'll need a networking preflight checklist before handing off to SRE for validation. Suggest:
- confirm subnet IP available (no overlap)
- firewall rules: allow 6443 from CI, 22 from infra VPN, and app ports from loadgen
- NAT egress rules and routes to peering
- BGP advert (if required) and route priorities

cheng: Also add the quota command snippet for GCP console and support ticket body:

```bash
# check current accelerator quota
gcloud compute regions describe europe-west3 --format='json(quotas)' | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric|test("GPUS"))'

# sample quota increase body for console
{
  "quotaChange": [{"metric":"GPUS","limit":32}],
  "reason":"Temporary capacity for customer bring-up - see INF-4521"
}
```

anika: I'll file the ticket now and ping the cloud rep. ETA for quota approval historically is 48-72h for non-reserved, longer for pinned capacity (5-10 business days) — flagging that to stakeholders.

mike: Tagging @product to set expectations: if pinned capacity can't be guaranteed, we will fallback to multi-region routing and a reduced soak plan.

anika: Filed. Ticket created INF-4521 with initial quota request and network checklist. Linked docs: runbook/bringups/eu-west3-v1 and a cost estimate.

mike: Cost note — estimate per A100-80GB on-demand: $6.50/hr (varies) — 32 GPUs for 2 weeks (14*24h) ~= $174k raw compute. We should bake a cost cap or approvals for > $10k/day.

cheng: For cost-savings: request preemptible/spot fallback for soak and use sustained use discounts only if we go long. Also enable local NVMe ephemeral if job needs fast checkpointing.

ops-oncall: Once quota is approved, steps for handoff:
1) infra creates bringup VPC and reserved instance templates
2) deploy autoscaler config (min nodes 0, target pods per gpu)
3) run health probes and sample inference dataset (10k samples)
4) SRE validates latency SLOs and token-cost metrics
5) signoff meeting with product + security

anika: Assigning tasks: quota request (me), network preflight (cheng), VPC + IAM prep (sarah), cost approvals (mike). I'll update INF-4521 with assignees and target dates.

sarah: Quick note on security: for private deployment tests, use customer-managed model artifacts and ensure no model weights leave KMS-protected GCS bucket. Enable object-level audit logs for the bring-up project.

mike: Thanks. If cloud rep accepts pinned capacity, we'll confirm exact start time and run the soak. If not, we pivot to staged soak with 8 -> 16 -> 32 over 3 days and use multi-region routing.

anika: Will update thread when quota status changes. Leaving the SOAK runbook checklist in INF-4521. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: quota-status INF-4521 updated: pending cloud rep acknowledgement.

mike: Great. End-to-end owner: anika. Please post when quota is approved and when the reservation is confirmed.

cheng: Also, if we get partial approvals, prewire the autoscaler with warm pools to avoid cold-start GPU allocation delays.

mike: Perfect. Closing notes: this thread is the live coordination log for EU bring-up GPU capacity. Keep comments short and tag infra-bot for ticket updates.
